- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00–0.33) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below prior high or adjust downward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days or apply 1–2% dampening factor.
